MATHEMATICS — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #13
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: MATHEMATICS
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What is the next number in the pattern 2, 8, 14, 20, ...? (1 mark)
   A. 26
   B. 27
   C. 32
   D. 25

2. What is the total value of the digit 1 in 1,523? (1 mark)
   A. 1
   B. 10,000
   C. 100
   D. 1,000

3. Which of these is a factor of 36? (1 mark)
   A. 8
   B. 7
   C. 9
   D. 5

4. What number is the Roman numeral VIII? (1 mark)
   A. 2
   B. 8
   C. 1
   D. 3

5. Which is the smallest number: 605, 560, 650, 506? (1 mark)
   A. 650
   B. 605
   C. 506
   D. 560

6. How many times do you need to regroup when you add 3,425 + 2,318? (1 mark)
   A. 0
   B. 3
   C. 2
   D. 1

7. How many times do you need to regroup when you add 1,234 + 4,321? (1 mark)
   A. 3
   B. 1
   C. 0
   D. 2

8. Work out 32 × 21. (1 mark)
   A. 672
   B. 662
   C. 96
   D. 682

9. What is 7 × 100? (1 mark)
   A. 70
   B. 7,000
   C. 700
   D. 107

10. What is 58 ÷ 4? (1 mark)
   A. 13 remainder 6
   B. 14 remainder 3
   C. 14 remainder 2
   D. 15 remainder 2

11. A rectangle is cut into 10 equal parts and 7 of the parts are shaded. What fraction of the rectangle is shaded? (1 mark)
   A. 7/3
   B. 3/10
   C. 7/10
   D. 10/7

12. Which fraction of an hour is 15 minutes? (1 mark)
   A. 1/3
   B. 3/4
   C. 1/4
   D. 1/2

13. In the fraction 7/8, what does the numerator 7 tell us? (1 mark)
   A. How many equal parts the whole has
   B. How many of the equal parts are taken
   C. The size of each part in centimetres
   D. The number of wholes

14. Change 4 3/8 to an improper fraction. (1 mark)
   A. 36/8
   B. 35/8
   C. 32/8
   D. 7/8

15. Ksh 12.50 means (1 mark)
   A. 12 shillings and 5 cents
   B. 1 shilling and 250 cents
   C. 12 shillings and 50 cents
   D. 125 shillings

16. Which decimal is the same as 3/4? (1 mark)
   A. 0.3
   B. 0.75
   C. 3.4
   D. 0.34

17. What is the total value of the digit 9 in 3.09? (1 mark)
   A. 0.009
   B. 9
   C. 0.09
   D. 0.9

18. Which pair are like terms? (1 mark)
   A. 2x and 2y
   B. 4 and 4z
   C. 3a and 5b
   D. 3a and 5a

19. A rectangle is 9 cm long and 4 cm wide. What is its perimeter? (1 mark)
   A. 36 cm
   B. 28 cm
   C. 26 cm
   D. 13 cm

20. A pencil starts at the 2 cm mark on a ruler and ends at the 9 cm mark. How long is the pencil? (1 mark)
   A. 11 cm
   B. 8 cm
   C. 9 cm
   D. 7 cm

21. An L-shaped garden has sides of 6 m, 2 m, 3 m, 2 m, 3 m and 4 m. What is its perimeter? (1 mark)
   A. 19 m
   B. 24 m
   C. 18 m
   D. 20 m

22. Change 400 cm to metres and centimetres. (1 mark)
   A. 5 m
   B. 4 m
   C. 4 m 50 cm
   D. 40 cm

23. Wanjiku says the area of a rectangle with 4 rows and 6 columns is 10 square units. Her mistake is that she (1 mark)
   A. counted the corners
   B. forgot to use a ruler
   C. added instead of multiplying
   D. multiplied instead of adding

24. A rectangle is made of 4 rows with 6 unit squares in each row. What is its area? (1 mark)
   A. 10 square units
   B. 28 square units
   C. 24 square units
   D. 20 square units

25. One layer of a cuboid has 15 blocks and there are 3 layers. What is the volume? (1 mark)
   A. 18 blocks
   B. 45 blocks
   C. 60 blocks
   D. 42 blocks

26. A cuboid is 5 blocks long, 5 blocks wide and 5 blocks high. What is its volume? (1 mark)
   A. 15 blocks
   B. 125 blocks
   C. 130 blocks
   D. 25 blocks

27. One layer of a cuboid has 20 blocks and there are 4 layers. What is the volume? (1 mark)
   A. 100 blocks
   B. 76 blocks
   C. 80 blocks
   D. 24 blocks

28. What is 7 1/2 L − 3 3/4 L? (1 mark)
   A. 3 1/2 L
   B. 4 1/4 L
   C. 3 3/4 L
   D. 4 L

29. How many minutes does the minute hand take to go once round the clock face? (1 mark)
   A. 30 minutes
   B. 12 minutes
   C. 24 minutes
   D. 60 minutes

30. What is 4 h 35 min + 3 h 40 min? (1 mark)
   A. 8 h 25 min
   B. 8 h 5 min
   C. 7 h 15 min
   D. 8 h 15 min

31. Why do people prepare a shopping list? (1 mark)
   A. To make shops close early
   B. To buy as many things as possible
   C. To avoid using money
   D. To remember everything and not spend more than they have

32. A shopping list has three items costing Ksh 650, Ksh 800 and Ksh 1,900. What is the total cost? (1 mark)
   A. Ksh 3,250
   B. Ksh 3,360
   C. Ksh 3,450
   D. Ksh 3,350

33. A shopping list has three items costing Ksh 240, Ksh 160 and Ksh 350. What is the total cost? (1 mark)
   A. Ksh 850
   B. Ksh 760
   C. Ksh 650
   D. Ksh 750

34. Kip faces East and makes a quarter turn anticlockwise. Which way does he face now? (1 mark)
   A. East
   B. North
   C. South
   D. West

35. Which object does NOT have a right angle at its corners? (1 mark)
   A. A door
   B. A window
   C. A round plate
   D. A book

36. How many right angles make a full turn? (1 mark)
   A. 1
   B. 2
   C. 4
   D. 3

37. What is the next shape in the pattern square, triangle, square, triangle, square, ...? (1 mark)
   A. Circle
   B. Rectangle
   C. Triangle
   D. Square

38. In the pattern blue square, orange square, blue square, orange square, and so on, what colour is the 6th square? (1 mark)
   A. Green
   B. Red
   C. Blue
   D. Orange

39. What is raw data? (1 mark)
   A. A picture of data
   B. Data written in a table
   C. Data that has been collected but not yet arranged
   D. Data that is wrong

40. What is data? (1 mark)
   A. A unit of time
   B. A kind of shape
   C. A measuring tape
   D. Information that we collect

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. A jerrycan holds 5 L. Musa pours out 2 1/2 L. How much is left in the jerrycan? (2 marks)

42. Find 3/4 of 12 counters. Explain each step. (3 marks)

43. A triangle has two equal sides. How many lines of symmetry does it have? Explain how you can check. (3 marks)

44. Start at 10,000 and subtract 1,500 each time. Write the first five numbers of the pattern. (3 marks)

45. Work out 6 1/4 kg − 2 3/4 kg. (3 marks)

46. The table shows mango 4, banana 3, orange 2 and pawpaw 1. How many pupils did not choose mango? (2 marks)

47. Ten pupils were asked their favourite fruit and the answers were: mango, banana, mango, orange, banana, mango, pawpaw, mango, banana, orange. (a) Show the data in a tally table. (b) Which fruit is the most popular? (c) How many more pupils chose mango than orange? (5 marks)

48. Divide 91 by 7 and check by multiplication. (3 marks)

49. A water tank holds 1,000 litres. Each day the family uses 125 litres. Write the amount left after 1, 2 and 3 days. (3 marks)

50. A shopping list has 3 packets of rice at Ksh 130 each, 2 bottles of oil at Ksh 250 each and 1 tin of tomatoes at Ksh 60. Find the total cost. (4 marks)

51. An L-shaped garden has sides of 6 m, 2 m, 3 m, 2 m, 3 m and 4 m. Find its perimeter. (3 marks)

52. Change 3.4 m to centimetres. (2 marks)

53. Change 150 minutes to hours and minutes, and change 35 days to weeks. (3 marks)

54. Explain why the digit carried from the tens column must be added in the hundreds column when adding 3,568 + 2,276. (3 marks)

55. Write the next three numbers in the pattern 2,000, 2,300, 2,600, 2,900. (3 marks)

56. Start at 1,500 and add 1,000 each time to write a pattern of five numbers. State the rule. (3 marks)

57. Write three reasons why we prepare a shopping list. (3 marks)

58. Arrange these prices from the cheapest to the most expensive: Ksh 8.25, Ksh 8.05, Ksh 8.50, Ksh 7.99. (3 marks)

59. Wanjiru saves Ksh 250 every week. Write how much she has saved after 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 weeks. State the rule. (3 marks)

60. Wafula has 20 goats. One fifth of them are brown. How many goats are brown? Show your working. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
MATHEMATICS — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #13 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — 26
   The rule is add 6. 20 + 6 = 26.

2. D — 1,000
   The digit 1 is in the thousands place, so its total value is 1 × 1,000 = 1,000.

3. C — 9
   36 ÷ 9 = 4 with nothing left over, so 9 is a factor of 36. The others leave a remainder.

4. B — 8
   VIII stands for 8.

5. C — 506
   Compare the digits from the left. The smallest number is 506.

6. D — 1
   Check each column from the right for a total of 10 or more, remembering the carried digit. 3,425 + 2,318 needs 1 regrouping.

7. C — 0
   Check each column from the right for a total of 10 or more, remembering the carried digit. 1,234 + 4,321 needs 0 regroupings.

8. A — 672
   32 × 1 = 32 and 32 × 20 = 640. 32 + 640 = 672.

9. C — 700
   Multiplying by 100 moves each digit two places to the left, so 7 × 100 = 700.

10. C — 14 remainder 2
   4 × 14 = 56 and 58 − 56 = 2. So 58 ÷ 4 = 14 remainder 2. Check: 14 × 4 + 2 = 58.

11. C — 7/10
   The whole has 10 equal parts and 7 are shaded, so 7/10 is shaded.

12. C — 1/4
   15 × 4 = 60, so 15 minutes is one quarter of an hour.

13. B — How many of the equal parts are taken
   The numerator is the top number. In 7/8 it says that 7 parts are taken.

14. B — 35/8
   4 × 8 = 32 and 32 + 3 = 35. The denominator stays 8, so the answer is 35/8.

15. C — 12 shillings and 50 cents
   The digits after the decimal point are the cents. Ksh 12.50 is 12 shillings and 50 cents.

16. B — 0.75
   3/4 = 75/100 = 0.75.

17. C — 0.09
   The digit 9 is in the hundredths place, so its total value is 0.09.

18. D — 3a and 5a
   Like terms have the same letter. 3a and 5a both have the letter a.

19. C — 26 cm
   Perimeter = 9 + 4 + 9 + 4 = 26 cm.

20. D — 7 cm
   Subtract the start from the end: 9 − 2 = 7 cm.

21. D — 20 m
   Add every side: 6 + 2 + 3 + 2 + 3 + 4 = 20 m.

22. B — 4 m
   400 ÷ 100 = 4 remainder 0. So 400 cm = 4 m.

23. C — added instead of multiplying
   Area is 4 × 6 = 24 square units. She added 4 + 6.

24. C — 24 square units
   Area = rows × columns = 4 × 6 = 24 square units.

25. B — 45 blocks
   Volume = blocks in one layer × layers = 15 × 3 = 45 blocks.

26. B — 125 blocks
   One layer has 5 × 5 = 25 blocks. There are 5 layers, so the volume is 25 × 5 = 125 blocks.

27. C — 80 blocks
   Volume = blocks in one layer × layers = 20 × 4 = 80 blocks.

28. C — 3 3/4 L
   Work with the whole litres first and then the parts. 7 1/2 L − 3 3/4 L = 3 3/4 L.

29. D — 60 minutes
   The minute hand takes one hour, which is 60 minutes.

30. D — 8 h 15 min
   Add the minutes and hours, then change 60 minutes into 1 hour. The answer is 8 h 15 min.

31. D — To remember everything and not spend more than they have
   A list helps us remember what we need and plan our spending.

32. D — Ksh 3,350
   Add the three costs: 650 + 800 + 1,900 = 3,350.

33. D — Ksh 750
   Add the three costs: 240 + 160 + 350 = 750.

34. B — North
   Going clockwise the order is North, East, South, West. Going anticlockwise it is North, West, South, East. East followed by a quarter turn anticlockwise gives North.

35. C — A round plate
   A round plate has a curved edge and no corners, so no right angles.

36. C — 4
   A full turn is four quarter turns, and each quarter turn is a right angle.

37. C — Triangle
   The pattern alternates between a square and a triangle, so a triangle comes next.

38. D — Orange
   The colours alternate blue, orange. Squares 2, 4 and 6 are orange.

39. C — Data that has been collected but not yet arranged
   Raw data is untidy information straight from collection.

40. D — Information that we collect
   Data is information such as counts or names that we collect to answer questions.

SECTION B
----
41. (2 marks)
   Answer: 2 1/2 L
   Working / marking points: 5 − 2 1/2 = 2 1/2. 1 mark for the subtraction and 1 mark for the unit.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: 9 counters. 12 ÷ 4 = 3 counters in one quarter; 3 × 3 = 9.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for dividing by the denominator, 1 mark for multiplying by the numerator, 1 mark for the answer.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: One line of symmetry. Fold it from the top corner to the middle of the base and the two halves match.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for one, 1 mark for the fold, 1 mark for the halves matching.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: 10,000, 8,500, 7,000, 5,500, 4,000
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the correct rule and 2 marks for the numbers.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: 3 1/2 kg
   Working / marking points: Change 6 1/4 to 5 5/4 (1 mark); wholes 5 − 2 = 3 and quarters 5/4 − 3/4 = 1/2 (1 mark); answer 3 1/2 kg (1 mark).

46. (2 marks)
   Answer: 6 pupils
   Working / marking points: 4 + 3 + 2 + 1 = 10 pupils; 10 − 4 = 6 (1 mark for the total, 1 mark for the answer).

47. (5 marks)
   Answer: (a) mango 4, banana 3, orange 2, pawpaw 1 (total 10) (b) mango (c) 4 − 2 = 2 pupils
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for a correct table with title and headings, 1 mark for correct tallies and totals, 1 mark for (b), 1 mark for (c).

48. (3 marks)
   Answer: 13. Check: 13 × 7 = 91.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 7 × 13, 1 mark for 13, 1 mark for the check.

49. (3 marks)
   Answer: 875 litres, 750 litres, 625 litres
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct amount.

50. (4 marks)
   Answer: Ksh 950
   Working / marking points: 3 × 130 = 390 (1 mark); 2 × 250 = 500 (1 mark); 390 + 500 + 60 (1 mark); Ksh 950 (1 mark).

51. (3 marks)
   Answer: 20 m
   Working / marking points: 6 + 2 + 3 + 2 + 3 + 4 = 20 m. 2 marks for adding all six sides, 1 mark for the unit.

52. (2 marks)
   Answer: 340 cm
   Working / marking points: 3 m = 300 cm and 0.4 m = 40 cm (1 mark). 300 + 40 = 340 cm (1 mark).

53. (3 marks)
   Answer: 150 minutes = 2 hours 30 minutes. 35 days = 5 weeks.
   Working / marking points: 150 ÷ 60 = 2 remainder 30 (1 mark for 2 h 30 min); 35 ÷ 7 = 5 (1 mark for 5 weeks); 1 mark for division working.

54. (3 marks)
   Answer: Ten tens make one hundred, so the extra 1 hundred must be counted with the hundreds. If it is left out the answer will be 100 too small.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for saying ten tens make a hundred, 1 mark for the carried digit being added in the next column, 1 mark for the effect of leaving it out.

55. (3 marks)
   Answer: 3,200, 3,500, 3,800 (rule: add 300)
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the rule and 2 marks for the three correct numbers.

56. (3 marks)
   Answer: 1,500, 2,500, 3,500, 4,500, 5,500. Rule: add 1,000.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the rule and 2 marks for five correct terms (1 mark for three or four).

57. (3 marks)
   Answer: To remember everything we need; to buy only what is needed; to avoid spending more than we have.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each sensible reason, up to 3 marks.

58. (3 marks)
   Answer: Ksh 7.99, Ksh 8.05, Ksh 8.25, Ksh 8.50
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 7.99 first and 2 marks for the correct order of the rest.

59. (3 marks)
   Answer: 250, 500, 750, 1,000, 1,250. Rule: add 250.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the rule and 2 marks for correct numbers.

60. (3 marks)
   Answer: 4 goats
   Working / marking points: 20 ÷ 5 = 4 (2 marks) and 1 × 4 = 4 goats (1 mark).
